title: Effect of different chelating agents and irrigation activation techniques on apical irrigant extrusion in simulated immature permanent tooth models: an in vitro study.
abstract: Background: This in vitro study evaluated the effects of chelating agents and irrigation activation techniques on apical irrigant extrusion in simulated immature permanent teeth with open apices. Methods: A total of 72 single-rooted human teeth with standardized open apices were randomly assigned to eight groups (n = 9) based on the chelating agent used-17% ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) or 9% etidronic acid (HEDP)-and the irrigation technique applied: conventional needle irrigation (CNI) using a 30-gauge side-vented needle, passive ultrasonic irrigation (PUI), photon-induced photoacoustic streaming (PIPS), or shock wave-enhanced emission photoacoustic streaming (SWEEPS). The Myers and Montgomery model was used to quantify apical extrusion. Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U test were used for statistical analyses. Results: All experimental groups exhibited apical irrigant extrusion to varying degrees. In the EDTA subgroups, activation techniques (PUI, PIPS, and SWEEPS) resulted in significantly higher extrusion levels compared to EDTA-CNI. HEDP groups demonstrated significantly lower extrusion overall, and no statistically significant differences were observed among the different activation methods. Comparisons between corresponding EDTA and HEDP groups revealed that HEDP consistently produced less extrusion than EDTA when paired with the same activation technique. title: Influence of third molar eruption status on the biomechanical environment of the temporomandibular joint: An in silico evaluation.
abstract: Third molar (M3) may potentially cause occlusal interference, disrupt occlusal balance, alter temporomandibular joint (TMJ) loading, and impair the functional homeostasis of the stomatognathic system. This study conducted finite element method (FEM) on seven typical M3 conditions, analyzed its effects on occlusal and joint loading, and built an analytic biomechanical model to explore the regulatory mechanism of mandibular morphological parameters. Results revealed that (1) the presence of M3 would elevate TMJ functional load for all seven cases, in comparison to congenital absence case (control model [CM]). (2) Moreover, both occlusally functional (four erupted) and non-occluded (three impacted) cases of M3 presence could shift bite force to the posterior dentition and TMJ. (3) With constant masticatory muscle force, greater relative occlusal plane height (h) and length (L) would reduce TMJ loading. However, the load trends between dentition and TMJ could be reversed in consideration of periodontal ligament (PDL) negative feedback, wherein the load tendency is consistent with clinical data. In conclusion, the M3 presence would hinder the dispersion of occlusal forces in the stomatognathic system, and consequently aggravate stress environments in TMJ. The extraction of M3 could be potentially beneficial for alleviating the stress situation in TMJ due to the increase of relative occlusal plane height.

title: Comparison of piezosurgery vs. conventional bone chisel for extraction of impacted mandibular third molars with root-canal intimacy: a retrospective cohort study with CBCT-based preoperative planning.
abstract: Objective: To compare clinical outcomes of piezosurgery vs. conventional chisel for extracting impacted mandibular third molars (IMTMs) with roots adjacent to the inferior alveolar nerve canal (IANC) under identical CBCT-based planning, isolating the ultrasonic osteotome's incremental benefit beyond shared imaging. Methods: A retrospective comparative cohort study was conducted using the clinical data of 126 patients with IMTMs whose tooth roots were closely adjacent to the IANC and who were treated in the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery at our hospital between September 2025 and May 2026. All patients underwent CBCT three-dimensional reconstruction before the operation to evaluate the anatomical structure and formulate the surgical plan. The patients were divided into the piezosurgery (n = 63) and conventional surgery (n = 63) groups. The conventional surgery group underwent traditional bone chiseling and crown splitting for extraction, while the piezosurgery group underwent extraction using the ultrasonic bone knife minimally invasive technique. The operation time, intraoperative blood loss, pain visual analogue scale (VAS) scores at different time points after surgery, degree of facial swelling, degree of mouth opening limitation, and complication occurrence rate were compared between the two groups. title: Impacted Permanent Teeth in the Mixed Dentition: Pediatric Diagnosis, Surgical Exposure, and Orthodontic Traction.
abstract: Permanent-tooth impaction during the mixed dentition is time-sensitive because eruption potential, root formation, arch space, and relationships with adjacent structures change during growth. This comprehensive narrative review evaluated evidence concerning pediatric diagnosis, interception, surgical exposure, orthodontic traction, treatment failure, and post-treatment outcomes. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through August 2026, with supplementary targeted searching. Diagnosis should integrate eruption symmetry and progression, space conditions, tooth-specific warning signs, and clinically directed imaging. Barrier removal and space provision may permit spontaneous eruption in favorable immature teeth, whereas primary-canine extraction may benefit selected palatal displacements but is not uniformly predictive. When definitive treatment is required, surgical access and orthodontic mechanics should be designed together. Evidence does not establish a universally superior exposure technique; tissue management, attachment placement, traction direction, and anchorage should follow anatomy and the intended eruption pathway. A defined path, usable space, stable anchorage, and staged movement away from vulnerable structures are more defensible than prescribing a named appliance or universal force threshold. title: Asymmetry of Maxillary and Mandibular Dentoalveolar Structures, Palatal Rugae Depth, and Two-Dimensional Projected Maxillary Sinus Area in Unilateral Maxillary Buccal and Palatal Canine Impactions.
abstract: Objectives: The aim of this study was to investigate the dentoalveolar, palatal rugae, and maxillary sinus asymmetry associated with unilateral maxillary buccal and palatal canine impactions. Materials And Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included pretreatment records of 59 patients aged between 13 and 17 years (17 with buccally impacted canines, 20 with palatally impacted canines, and 22 controls). Maxillary and mandibular dentoalveolar measurements were obtained from three-dimensional digital models using OrthoAnalyzer software. The depth of the first palatal rugae was measured using Autodesk Fusion, whereas the two-dimensional projected maxillary sinus area was measured on panoramic radiographs using SketchAndCalc software. Asymmetry was quantified as the absolute difference between the right and left side measurements, and the magnitude of asymmetry was compared among the study groups. Results: In the intergroup comparisons, statistically significant differences were observed in the asymmetry values of the maxillary central and lateral incisors, as well as in the first palatal rugae depth (p < 0.001, p = 0.006, and p = 0.007, respectively). The highest asymmetry values were found in the palatal group, followed by the buccal and control groups. title: Diabetic Patients' Awareness and Knowledge of the Association Between Apical Periodontitis and Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Backgrounds/Objectives: The objective of this study was to evaluate diabetic patients' knowledge and awareness regarding the association between diabetes mellitus and apical periodontitis and to examine demographic and clinical factors associated with knowledge and awareness scores. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted involving 504 patients with diabetes who attended the Obesity and Diabetes Research and Application Center between September 2025 and February 2026. Data regarding demographic characteristics, clinical status, and knowledge/awareness of the DM-apical periodontitis link were collected via a structured questionnaire. Statistical analyses were performed using the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn's multiple comparison test, the Mann-Whitney U test, and Spearman's correlation analysis (p < 0.05). Separate multiple linear regression models were also used to identify factors independently associated with knowledge and awareness scores. Results: The majority of participants were aged 51-80 (76.0%), female (59.1%) and had completed primary education (41.5%, n = 209). While 84% acknowledged the need for regular dental check-ups, 49.1% visited a dentist only for emergencies, and 85.9% lacked prior knowledge of apical periodontitis. title: Guided bone regeneration with polytetrafluoroethylene titanium-reinforced membrane, CAD/CAM semi-occlusive titanium mesh and CAD/CAM occlusive titanium foil in partially atrophic arches: A comparative randomised controlled trial with 3-year follow-up.
journal: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)
abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the effectiveness of three distinct guided bone regeneration devices, namely non-resorbable polytetrafluoroethylene membrane, semi-occlusive CAD/CAM titanium mesh and occlusive CAD/CAM titanium foil, over a 3-year period, focusing on clinical and radiographic outcomes. Materials And Methods: Twenty-seven partially edentulous patients with alveolar atrophy requiring guided bone regeneration for implant placement were enrolled and randomly allocated to one of three treatment groups (polytetrafluoroethylene, mesh or foil). Surgical time and surgical satisfaction were assessed and compared among the groups. The present study reports the 3-year clinical outcomes update, including marginal bone loss and complications. Results: Mean marginal bone loss at 3 years was 0.82 ± 0.46 mm in the polytetrafluoroethylene group, 0.95 ± 0.36 mm in the mesh group and 0.92 ± 0.61 mm in the foil group, with no significant association between device type. Six bone augmentation-related complications occurred, with no significant difference among groups (P = 0.842). Five implant-related complications were recorded among 60 implants (P = 0.730), including one implant failure; no prosthetic failures occurred. Smoking was significantly associated with greater marginal bone loss at 3 years (P = 0.015). title: AI-driven opportunistic screening for carotid atheroma calcification on dental radiographs.
abstract: To develop a labeled image dataset of suspected carotid artery calcifications (CACs) on dental panoramic radiographs (PRs) and to propose a deep learning-based framework for their automated detection and segmentation. A retrospective dataset comprising 19,205 PRs obtained from our institution (between 2015 and 2023) was analyzed. After manual labeling, 372 images showing CACs and 322 controls were included. A hybrid architecture combining FasTVit, AttentionNet, and DC-UNet was implemented for classification, detection, and segmentation. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, the Dice coefficient, intersection over union (IoU), and area under the curve (AUC). The study evaluated two scenarios: one in which detection and segmentation were performed after classification, and another in which the classification was omitted. The classification model achieved an accuracy of 0.8780, a precision of 0.8779, a recall of 0.8795, and a specificity of, 0.8795. Incorporating the classification step improved precision from 0.48 to 0.93, accuracy from 0.79 to 0.97, and specificity from 0.75 to 0.98. The final framework achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.96. The proposed hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) framework showed promising internal performance for the opportunistic detection and localization of radiographic findings suggestive of CACs on PRs. title: Vital Pulp Treatment: A Minimally Invasive Approach in Daily Practice for Managing Caries-related Pulpal Disease.
abstract: Vital pulp treatments, particularly pulpotomy, have demonstrated outcomes similar to root canal therapy while reducing biological, technical, and economic burdens. Their success, however, relies on accurate assessment of pulpal status, an inherently challenging task due to the limitations of current diagnostic methods, as well as rigorous clinical execution. This requires careful removal of carious tissue, appropriate management of pulp exposure, and achievement of proper hemostasis, since the ability to control bleeding determines whether a more invasive treatment is indicated. Over the exposed pulp, a hydraulic calcium silicate cement must be placed, followed by a durable and bacteria-tight coronal restoration to ensure long-term prognosis.

title: Transforming Children's Oral Health Worldwide: Three Decades of the Colgate Bright Smiles, Bright Futures® Prevention Program.
journal: Compendium of continuing education in dentistry (Jamesburg, N.J. : 1995)
abstract: The Colgate Bright Smiles, Bright Futures (BSBF) prevention program is a global oral health program designed to improve children's oral health through integrated prevention, education, community engagement, and partnerships with public, private, and academic organizations. As Colgate-Palmolive's flagship social impact initiative, the program was launched in North America in 1991 and rapidly expanded to countries around the world in 1994. It has since been successfully integrated into and adapted across diverse local cultures, healthcare systems, schools, ministries of health, and community organizations. The program aims to improve oral health literacy, promote beneficial oral health behaviors, and expand access to preventive services, including free dental screenings and treatment referrals. By strengthening the capacity of communities and oral health professionals to promote good oral health behaviors, combat early childhood caries, and connect underserved children to a dental home, the program seeks to advance health equity and improve oral health outcomes for children worldwide. In this report, the authors synthesized evidence from published literature, program evaluations, internal reports, partner documentation, and implementation records to examine the implementation, expansion, partnerships, sustainability, and outcomes of BSBF. title: Piezocision-Assisted Orthodontic Treatment for Accelerating Mandibular Anterior Alignment in Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Introduction: Piezocision is a minimally invasive surgical adjunct used to accelerate orthodontic tooth movements. However, evidence regarding its effectiveness in anterior mandibular alignment remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between piezocision-assisted orthodontic treatment and the rate and time required for mandibular anterior decrowding. Materials And Methods: This retrospective observational cohort study analyzed 60 eligible patient records, comprising 30 (50.0%) patients treated with piezocision-assisted fixed orthodontics and 30 (50.0%) treated with conventional fixed orthodontics. The primary outcome was the time to anterior mandibular reduction of crowding. Secondary outcomes included decrowding rate, total treatment duration, change in Little's Irregularity Index (LII), number of visits, and adverse events. Between-group comparisons were performed using appropriate parametric and nonparametric tests, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results: The median time to mandibular anterior decrowding was 112 days in the piezocision group compared with 168 days in the conventional treatment group (p < 0.001). The rate of decrowding was significantly higher in the piezocision group than in the conventional treatment group (1.85 ± 0.42 vs. 1.12 ± 0.35 mm/month; p < 0.001), while total active treatment duration was significantly shorter (14.2 ± 3.1 vs. 19.6 ± 4.0 months; p < 0.001). title: The Central Role of O-GlcNAcylation in Regulating Macrophages in the Pathogenesis of Periodontitis.
abstract: Background: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by dental plaque biofilm, characterized primarily by dysregulated host immune-inflammatory responses and progressive alveolar bone resorption, in which the dynamic M1/M2 polarization of macrophages serves as a pivotal regulatory factor. O-GlcNAcylation is a nutrient-sensitive post translational modification, and the relationship between O-GlcNAcylation and periodontitis needs further elucidation. Methods: This article systematically reviews recent advances concerning the regulatory role of O-GlcNAcylation in macrophage-mediated periodontitis pathogenesis. Particular emphasis is placed on the bidirectional dose and site-specific effects of O-GlcNAcylation on macrophage polarization. In addition, the molecular mechanisms underlying pathological O-GlcNAcylation-mediated aggravated alveolar bone loss in diabetes-associated periodontitis are summarized. Results: Existing evidence identifies O-GlcNAcylation as a critical molecular hub linking metabolic derangements to periodontal osteoimmune destruction: it either potentiates M1-like pro-inflammatory responses and osteoclastogenesis, or facilitates M2-like reparative phenotypes and periodontal bone regeneration. title: Deep learning-based classification of dental caries from intraoral photographs using ICDAS criteria.
abstract: Objectives: Dental caries remains a major global health burden, yet current artificial intelligence tools are often constrained by limited classification systems or rely on specialized imaging equipment unsuitable for self-examination. This study aims to develop and validate a deep learning-based approach using intraoral photographs to detect and classify dental caries using the full International Caries Detection and Assessment System (ICDAS) alongside modified ICDAS, merged ICDAS, and binary classification schemes. Methods: ICDAS scores were assigned through direct clinical examination. Two annotators independently examined each patient and compared their results. Disagreements were first resolved by joint re-examination. If consensus could not be reached, a third senior clinician examined the patient and made the final determination. A dataset of 1606 intraoral photographs was collected from volunteers aged five years and older across multiple clinics in China. The dataset was split into training, validation, and test sets at an 8:1:1 ratio at the patient level. The YOLOv12x and YOLOv8x architectures were trained and tested, with performance evaluated in terms of precision, recall, and mean average precision at 50% IoU (mAP50) with 95% confidence intervals. Gaussian blur was systematically applied to the test set at seven σ levels (0 to 11) to evaluate robustness. title: Efficacy of XP-Endo Finisher R, D-RaCe systems, and H-files in the retrieval of extruded gutta-percha from the periapical space.
abstract: Background: Overextension of gutta-percha (GP) beyond the apical foramen may impair periapical healing and complicate nonsurgical retreatment. This study compared the efficacy of XP-Endo Finisher R, D-RaCe, and H-files in retrieving overextended GP from the periapical space. Materials And Methods: In this in vitro study, sixty-nine extracted human premolars with straight single roots and canals were prepared up to ProTaper F3 and obturated with GP and AH26 sealer using lateral condensation. Overextension was simulated by intentionally extending an F2 GP cone 2 ± 0.5 mm beyond the apical foramen. Specimens were randomly assigned to XP-Endo Finisher R, H-file, and D-RaCe groups (n = 23 per group). Outcomes were classified as complete removal, attached residual, or displaced/detached material in the simulated periapical space. Descriptive statistics and Pearson's Chi-square test were used (P < 0.05). Results: Complete removal occurred in 10.1% (n = 7), attached residual in 40.6% (n = 28), and displaced/detached material in 49.3% (n = 34). No significant difference was found for complete removal versus nonremoval (P = 0.194). However, overall outcome distribution differed significantly among instruments (χ 2 = 20.842, P < 0.001). D-RaCe demonstrated the highest rate of complete removal, whereas H-files resulted in the highest frequency of apical displacement or detachment of the extruded material. title: Association of probing depth and crestal bone loss at implants: A long-term 5- to 20-year cohort study in periodontally stable patients.
journal: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)
abstract: Purpose: The aim of this long-term cohort study in periodontally stable patients with dental implants was to investigate the association between probing depth and peri-implant bone loss and compare outcomes between implants with machined versus rough surfaces. Materials And Methods: A total of 268 implants were inserted in 71 patients and restored with fixed crowns or partial dentures. All patients participated in a supportive periodontal therapy programme with recall intervals of 3 to 6 months over a follow-up period ranging from 5 to 20 years. Clinical parameters were recorded at each follow-up visit. Standardised intraoral radiographs were taken at baseline (immediately after superstructure insertion) and at 1, 3, 5, 10, 15 and 20 years thereafter. Results: Mean crestal bone loss between implant placement and superstructure insertion (baseline) was 0.99 ± 0.75 mm. During the loading phase, peri-implant bone loss increased to 1.60 ± 0.90 mm at the 20-year follow-up. Mixed-effects analysis showed no differences in bone loss between surface types except at the 15-year follow-up, when machined surfaces exhibited moderately greater bone loss (P = 0.026). title: Masticatory performance in mixed dentition children before and after dental treatment: an in vivo assessment using a two-coloured chewing gum mixing test.
abstract: Background: To evaluate the effects of dental treatment on masticatory performance and food preferences in children during the mixed dentition period using a two-coloured chewing gum test and a food preference questionnaire. Methods: This prospective clinical study included 100 children aged 6-9 years, categorized into three groups based on the Caries Assessment Spectrum and Treatment Index. Masticatory performance and food preferences were assessed before and three months after treatment. Masticatory performance was evaluated using a two-coloured chewing gum test (Vivident Fruit Swing) and analyzed by Variance of Hue (VOH) in ViewGum© software. At the same time, food preferences were assessed with a 30-item questionnaire. Posterior occlusal contacts, body mass index (BMI)-for-age z-scores, and pain scores were also recorded. Data were analyzed using R software, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Post-treatment VOH values decreased significantly in all groups (CAST 5, p < 0.001; CAST 6, p < 0.001; CAST 7, p = 0.024). Posterior occlusal contacts increased in CAST 5 and 6 but decreased in CAST 7 (p < 0.001). VOH correlated positively with MT/mt and negatively with FT/ft and occlusal contacts (p < 0.001). Preferences for hard and fibrous foods (e.g., carrot, walnut, apple, meat) increased, while rejection due to chewing pain decreased (p < 0.001). title: Deep learning for dental age assessment from panoramic radiographs: regression-based age estimation and threshold-based age classification.
abstract: Introduction And Objectives: Deep learning has significantly advanced medical image analysis by enabling automated extraction of complex imaging features with high predictive performance. In forensic dental age assessment, however, most artificial intelligence studies focus on either chronological age estimation or legal age threshold classification, limiting direct comparisons between predictive tasks. This study aimed to evaluate deep learning models for both continuous age estimation and judicial age threshold classification using panoramic radiographs, assessing their performance, robustness and potential applicability as decision-support tools in forensic practice. Materials And Methods: A dataset of 9,814 anonymised digital panoramic radiographs from individuals with known chronological age was retrospectively collected and standardised through image preprocessing. title: Alloplastic bone graft combined with injectable platelet-rich fibrin versus xenograft for horizontal ridge augmentation in the posterior mandible: a split-mouth randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Objectives: To compare 6-month horizontal bone gain and early postoperative morbidity between an alloplastic graft with injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF) and xenograft alone, both placed simultaneously with implants using the decompression technique in the posterior mandible. Materials And Methods: In this prospective split-mouth randomized controlled trial, 20 patients with bilateral posterior mandibular edentulism and insufficient horizontal bone width were enrolled. Each received a randomly assigned treatment: alloplastic graft with i-PRF (test) on one side and xenograft (control) on the other, both with simultaneous implant placement and a collagen membrane. The primary outcome was horizontal bone gain (6-month minus baseline) assessed by cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Secondary outcomes were postoperative edema, pain measured on a visual analog scale (VAS) from the first to the seventh postoperative days, and soft-tissue healing evaluated using the Landry index. title: Evaluation of antibiotic prescribing in dental practices in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and a comparison with national and international prescribing practices - a retrospective look at the situation in 2015.
abstract: Introduction: The aim of this study was to evaluate the antibiotic prescribing practices of dental practitioners and dental clinics in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania with regard to therapeutic and prophylactic indications, microbiological diagnostics, level of knowledge, and factors influencing prescribing behavior, to draw conclusions for antibiotic stewardship (ABS). Method: The study was conducted as a cross-sectional survey and included all private dental practices which could be contacted via the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania Dental Association, as well as university and hospital dental clinics. The questionnaire included sociodemographic data, therapeutic and prophylactic antibiotic prescriptions, selection of antibiotics, usage of microbiological diagnostics, knowledge levels, and factors influencing prescribing behavior. Data collection took place in 2015 via post. Results: Of 1,470 dentists contacted, 533 took part in the survey (response rate 36.3%). The majority stated that they prescribed 1-3 antibiotics per week. Clindamycin was the most commonly used antibiotic for odontogenic abscesses, apical periodontitis, peri-implantitis and osteomyelitis, followed by amoxicillin. title: Pulpal response following SDF application for deep carious lesions:An in vivo study.
abstract: Deep carious lesions often threaten pulpal vitality and limited evidence exists regarding the pulpal response to 38% silver diamine fluoride (SDF) in primary and permanent molars. Therefore, it is of interest to evaluate the pulpal response to 38% SDF in deep carious lesions of primary and permanent molars. Hence, a total of 70 molars (35 primary, 35 permanent) were treated with SDF following selective caries removal and monitored clinically and radiographically for 12 months. Most teeth maintained pulpal vitality, with overall success rates of 80% in primary molars and 85.7% in permanent molars. Failures were mainly associated with spontaneous pain or radiographic periapical changes during follow-up. Thus, we show that SDF is a minimally invasive and biologically compatible option for managing deep caries while preserving pulp vitality in both dentitions.

title: Assessment of antibiotic prescribing patterns and antimicrobial resistance awareness among dentists: a mixed-methods study.
abstract: Background: Antimicrobial resistance is a global "silent pandemic" with dentistry contributing 10%-12% of outpatient antibiotic use. In low- and middle-income countries such as India, the absence of context-specific national dental antibiotic guidelines, widespread over-the-counter antibiotic access, and diagnostic limitations complicate rational prescribing and antimicrobial stewardship. Methods: A sequential explanatory mixed method study was conducted over 12 months in Varanasi. The quantitative component analyzed 2,844 dental prescriptions across primary, secondary, and tertiary care settings. Prescribing appropriateness was assessed using international evidence-based guidelines from the American Dental Association and Faculty of General dental Practice (UK). The qualitative component included 30 in-depth interviews with dental practitioners, analyzed using inductive thematic analysis to explore determinants of prescribing behavior. Results: Antibiotics were prescribed in 73.1% of cases, of which 69.6% were inappropriate. High prescribing rates observed in conditions where antibiotics are generally not indicated, including irreversible pulpitis (73.3%), apical periodontitis (92.3%), and implant procedures (100%). title: Artificial intelligence for detecting C-shaped canals on dental radiographs: A systematic review and bayesian diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective: To evaluate AI-based identification of C-shaped canals across dental radiographic modalities, with an exploratory synthesis of conventional panoramic detection using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) reference labels. Methods: Seven sources were searched through August 12, 2026. Peer-reviewed original studies were appraised using QUADAS-3, STARD-AI, and GRADE. Binary panoramic estimates with CBCT reference and auditable counts were pooled using a Bayesian bivariate model nesting external centers within parent studies. Prospero: CRD420251046384. Results: Nine studies were included; three independent parent studies supplied five cohorts (899C-shaped and 953 non-C-shaped teeth). Pooled sensitivity was 0.918 (95 % credible interval [CrI], 0.837-0.962) and specificity 0.885 (0.588-0.969). Marginal model-implied new-parent-study prediction intervals were 0.716-0.981 and 0.219-0.993, respectively. Only one program provided multicenter external evaluation, with center-specific optimized thresholds. All selected estimates had high risk of bias. Certainty was low for sensitivity and very low for specificity. Conclusions: The sparse evidence does not establish dependable clinical performance. Predictive uncertainty and workflow limitations constrain transportability. Prospective evaluation of prespecified systems and clinical consequences is needed before implementation.

title: Immediate autotransplantation of an immature mandibular third molar into a second-molar socket with apical periodontitis: a 12-month case report.
abstract: Tooth autotransplantation can provide a biologic replacement option when a suitable donor tooth is available. A 20-year-old man with a non-restorable mandibular right second molar diagnosed with pulp necrosis and asymptomatic apical periodontitis underwent immediate autotransplantation of an immature mesioangular mandibular right third molar with approximately three-quarters root development and open apices. After extraction and thorough recipient-socket debridement, the donor tooth was transferred with an extra-alveolar time of <30 s and stabilized for 14 days. Pulp sensibility tests were negative at 14 days but positive at 6 and 12 months. At 12 months, the transplanted tooth was asymptomatic, clinically stable, and functional; periapical radiography showed surrounding bone healing, continued root development, and apical narrowing. This case illustrates the potential of autotransplantation as a conservative option for selected posterior tooth replacement despite pre-existing apical pathology at the recipient tooth.

title: Association Between Postoperative Symptom Severity and Oral Health-Related Quality of Life After Mandibular Third Molar Extraction.
abstract: Objectives: Third molar extraction of the mandible is considered to be among the most common forms of oral surgery, which is accompanied by post-surgery pain, swelling, and functional disabilities. The symptoms may affect patients' Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL). This research investigated the correlation between postoperative symptom severity and OHRQoL in mandibular third molar removal. Materials And Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 386 patients who presented to the oral and maxillofacial surgery outpatient departments. A structured questionnaire containing demographic data, the Postoperative Symptom Severity (PoSSe) scale, and the Oral Health Impact Profile (OHIP-14) was used to gather data. Pearson correlation, t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and multiple linear regression were used to identify predictors of OHRQoL. Results: The average scores of PoSSe and OHIP-14 were 41.0 and 42.2, respectively. A strong positive correlation was found between PoSSe and OHIP-14 scores (r = 0.58, p < 0.001), indicating lower OHRQoL as symptom severity increased. Women scored significantly higher than men on both PoSSe and OHIP-14 scales (p < 0.001). People aged 56 years and above indicated the highest symptom severity and poorest OHRQoL. PoSSe was the most potent indicator of OHRQoL (B = 0.420, p < 0.001), with age and sex following next. title: Intra-sulcular compound chamomile and lidocaine hydrochloride gel for procedural pain during ultrasonic scaling: a randomized, single-blind, split-mouth, sham-controlled superiority trial in adults with plaque-induced gingivitis.
abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate whether intra-sulcular application of a compound chamomile and lidocaine hydrochloride gel (Kami-Gel) reduces procedural pain during ultrasonic supragingival scaling in adults with plaque-induced gingivitis compared with a sham procedure. Materials And Methods: A single-center, randomized, single-blind, split-mouth, sham-controlled superiority trial was conducted involving 114 adults with plaque-induced gingivitis. Participants received a sequential split-mouth treatment. The test side received intra-sulcular application of Kami-Gel, while the control side received a sham application (mimicked injection). The primary outcome was procedural pain intensity measured on a 0-10 Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes included the number of pain complaints, procedural duration, patient satisfaction, and plaque index (PI). Safety was assessed immediately and at 24 h. Results: All 114 participants completed the study. Median VAS score was significantly lower in the test group (1.7 [IQR: 0.62-2.58]) than the control group (4.1 [IQR: 2.42-5.7]), with an estimated treatment difference of - 2.35 (95% CI: -3.0 to - 1.7)-the upper limit of which fell below the pre-specified superiority margin of - 1.2, confirming superiority (P < 0.001). The test group also demonstrated significantly fewer pain complaints (median 0 vs. 1), shorter procedural duration (median 10 vs. 12 min), and higher patient satisfaction (all P < 0.001). title: Advances and Future Perspectives on Chitosan-Based Hydrogels for Bone Regeneration in Periodontitis-Associated Defects.
abstract: Periodontitis-triggered alveolar bone loss is an irreversible pathological lesion that remains challenging to regenerate in clinical practice. Functionally modified chitosan (CS) hydrogels combine favorable biocompatibility, tunable biodegradability, intrinsic antibacterial activity, and immunomodulatory properties, rendering them promising scaffolds for the repair of inflammatory bone defects. This review summarizes advances over the past five years in the development of functionalized CS hydrogels for periodontitis-associated alveolar bone regeneration. We categorize and compare four mainstream modification strategies for CS: biomimetic structural design, inflammatory immunoregulation, stimuli-responsive controlled release, and mechanical microenvironment adaptation. Beyond hydrogels, chemically modified CS in diverse forms (membranes, bulk scaffolds, micro/nanoparticles, and surface coatings) is also discussed. Furthermore, we comprehensively elaborate on the core regenerative mechanisms of modified CS hydrogels, including antibacterial defense, immune microenvironment remodeling, osteogenic activation, and angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling. Unlike most previous reviews covering CS biomaterials, the present work specifically focuses on the challenges of bone regeneration under periodontitis-related inflammatory conditions, with a small set of other bone regeneration studies included as supporting references. title: Full (total) pulpotomy versus non-surgical root canal treatment for irreversible pulpitis: a human-led umbrella review with AI-assisted appraisal.
abstract: Objective: To evaluate systematic reviews and meta-analyses comparing vital pulp treatments (VPTs) with non-surgical root canal treatment (NSRCT) for irreversible pulpitis (IP) in permanent teeth, focusing on clinical/radiographic success and postoperative pain, and to compare AI (ChatGPT-4.1) with human reviewers for risk of bias (ROBIS) and methodological quality (AMSTAR-2). Materials And Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, EBSCO and Google Scholar were searched from inception to January 2026 according to PRISMA 2020. Predefined criteria guided screening and extraction. Two reviewers independently applied AMSTAR-2 and ROBIS; the same appraisals were repeated with ChatGPT-4.1 using identical inputs. Results: Of 641 records, 12 systematic reviews met the eligibility criteria; six incorporated quantitative synthesis/meta-analysis, whereas the remaining reviews used structured qualitative synthesis. Regarding the outcomes assessed, 2 reviews focused on postoperative pain, 7 on clinical/radiographic success, and 3 addressed both. All compared only one VPT technique -full pulpotomy- with NSRCT; no eligible reviews provided outcomes for other VPTs. The evidence ultimately drew on 11 unique primary studies. Across reviews, full pulpotomy often achieved short- to medium-term outcomes comparable to NSRCT. title: Long-term outcomes of a standardised interdisciplinary protocol for implant-prosthetic rehabilitation in patients with severe oligodontia associated with ectodermal dysplasia: A retrospective case series with a follow-up period of up to 30 years.
journal: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)
abstract: Purpose: Oral rehabilitation in patients with ectodermal dysplasia is complex due to severe oligodontia and extreme alveolar ridge atrophy. This retrospective case series aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of a standardised interdisciplinary protocol for the oral rehabilitation of patients with ectodermal dysplasia. Materials And Methods: 13 patients (8 men and 5 women; mean age 20.5 ± 1.9 years) with severe oligodontia (mean 18.4 ± 4.4 missing teeth) were included. The cohort included 12 cases of hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia and one case of Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome. The protocol consisted of orthodontic treatment until skeletal maturity, restoration of the vertical dimension of occlusion via fixed temporary restorations supported by natural teeth and/or interim implants, 3D bone reconstruction using autogenous bone (iliac crest or intraoral bone blocks) via the split bone block technique, and placement of dental implants followed by definitive prosthetic rehabilitation. Clinical and radiographic parameters were assessed over an observation period of 14.4 ± 7.0 years (median 13 years; range 5 to 30 years). Results: A total of 147 implants were placed (79 in the maxilla and 68 in the mandible). All patients were successfully rehabilitated with fixed implant-supported prosthetics. Three patients were lost to follow-up (non-attendance) after a mean observation period of 19.0 ± 3.6 years. The implant survival rate was 100% over the entire observation period. All grafts

title: Prevalence of temporomandibular disorder symptoms, anxiety and depression in military police officers.
abstract: Objective: To assess the prevalence of temporomandibular disorder (TMD)-related pain, anxiety, and depression among military police officers from Niteroi, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and to compare these outcomes with a civilian population. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 84 police officers treated at the Dental Service of the Military Police Hospital and 84 non-police officers treated at the School of Dentistry of Fluminense Federal University. Data were collected digitally using validated instruments: the TMD Pain Screener, the Symptom Questionnaire, and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. Statistical analyses were performed according to variable characteristics, with a significance level of 5%. Results: TMD-related pain was identified in 26.2% of police officers and 31.0% of civilians. No statistically significant differences were found between groups regarding anxiety or depression prevalence. In both groups, women showed a higher frequency of TMD symptoms (p < 0.05). Conclusion: Police officers and civilians showed similar TMD-related pain prevalence.

title: Barriers to and facilitators of access to geriatric oral healthcare in India: an ontological analysis.
abstract: Background: Oral health is a fundamental yet frequently neglected component of supportive and palliative care for older adults, directly influencing comfort, nutrition, and communication. Despite this, geriatric oral healthcare (GOHC) remains fragmented and poorly integrated into palliative care systems, especially in low- and middle-income countries such as India. This study applies an ontology-based approach to systematically examine barriers to and facilitators of access to GOHC and to identify neglected pathways relevant to supportive and palliative care. An ontology encompassing eight interrelated dimensions of access to GOHC was developed. Methods: A structured synthesis of peer-reviewed literature indexed in Scopus and PubMed was undertaken, and 100 eligible articles were mapped onto the ontology. Monad and theme maps were generated to assess patterns of research emphasis and gaps. Results: The findings indicate a strong research focus on financial and temporal barriers to physical access and on dentist-led preventive care for edentulism and dental caries. In contrast, promotive, rehabilitative, and palliative oral healthcare, virtual and home-based care models, non-dental and community-based providers, and conditions highly relevant to palliative care, including oral cancer and symptom-focused oral management, are substantially underrepresented. title: Automatic Detection of Dental Implant Brands and Exposure Status Using Deep Learning on Periapical Radiographs.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Dental implant technology has become the primary treatment modality for managing tooth loss in current clinical practice. Accurate identification of implant brands and their clinical exposure status have increasingly emerged as a critical issue in implant-related research and clinical diagnosis. Conventional approaches that rely on clinicians' experience are time-consuming and may lead to misclassification due to variations in image quality or subtle differences in implant design features across brands. Methods: This single-center study classified six categories combining two implant brands (3i and Xive) and three exposure statuses. A retrospective cohort of 497 patients (708 periapical radiographs, 928 implant instances) was partitioned using an 8:1:1 stratified ratio with strict patient-level independence. Following YOLOv8-based implant localization and ROI extraction, classification was evaluated across deep learning backbones using 5-fold cross-validation and compared against a panel of three dental specialists on a test set of 8 complex cases. Results: YOLOv8 achieved a precision of 99.39% and a sensitivity of 98.63% in the implant detection task. For the classification of implant brand and exposure status, EfficientNet-B3 achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 99.18 ± 0.85% (95% CI: [94.20%, 100.00%]) across 5-fold cross-validation, demonstrating competitive diagnostic performance alongside existing implant classification benchmarks in

title: Application of artificial intelligence in predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients: a scoping review.
abstract: Introduction: This scoping review aims to evaluate artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, for predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients and to identify methodological gaps limiting clinical translation. Methods: Reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across six electronic databases (PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library), grey literature, and citation tracking (Jan 1, 2018-June 1, 2025). Out of 880 identified records (312 duplicates removed; 568 screened), 56 full texts were evaluated, yielding 3 core clinical CBCT studies meeting strict eligibility criteria (Xu et al., 2024; Pirayesh et al., 2024; Zheng et al., 2025). Methodological quality and risk of bias were appraised using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Results: Reported performance for orthodontically induced inflammatory root resorption (OIIRR) ranged from 82.1% accuracy in small canine-induced resorption cohorts to >94% accuracy in larger grading frameworks. However, critical appraisal revealed a high risk of bias across all studies due to single-center retrospective designs, lack of independent external validation, and missing calibration metrics. Direct clinical evidence for AI prediction of gingival recession or orthodontic alveolar bone loss was insufficient within strict pre-cutoff parameters. title: Evaluation of the diagnostic performance of an implant marginal bone loss measurement method based on deep learning.
journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of the YOLOv8-pose model for automated measurement of mesial and distal peri-implant marginal bone loss on periapical radiographs. Methods: In this retrospective study, 162 images were divided into training (n = 144) and validation (n = 18) sets; 46 images formed an independent test set. Six anatomical key points were annotated and verified as the gold standard. The model was tested at thresholds of bone loss ≥0.5 mm, ≥1.0 mm, and ≥2.0 mm. F1-score was additionally calculated for each threshold. Results: At the 0.5 mm threshold, the model achieved 95.35% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% positive predictive value (PPV), and 90.7% mesial-distal diagnostic consistency. At the 1.0 mm threshold, sensitivity was 91.67%, specificity 82.14%, PPV 73.33%, and consistency 58.14%. At the 2.0 mm threshold, sensitivity dropped to 30.43%, while specificity remained high at 95.97%, with 53.85% PPV and 72.1% consistency. Median key point localization errors ranged from 0.76 mm to 1.05 mm, with no statistically significant difference among groups (P > 0.05). Conclusions: The YOLOv8-pose model shows excellent diagnostic performance, especially for early mild bone loss. This artificial intelligence tool serves as an auxiliary early-screening tool rather than a comprehensive diagnostic tool covering all severities of bone loss; it can assist clinicians in standardized, efficient, and early screening assessment of peri-implant diseases. title: Structural equation modeling of parental oral health literacy and orthodontic treatment needs in children.
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of parental oral health literacy on orthodontic treatment needs in children aged 8 to 10 years, using structural equation modeling. A representative population-based cross-sectional study was conducted with 739 children. Parents/legal guardians answered a sociodemographic questionnaire and the Brazilian Oral Health Literacy-Adult Questionnaire (BOHL-AQ). Orthodontic treatment needs were assessed by four calibrated examiners (Kappa > 0.80) using the dental aesthetic index (DAI). Structural equation modeling was performed to determine direct and indirect associations between the variables of the theoretical model (95% CI) using Mplus version 8.8. Orthodontic treatment needs were identified in 55.2% of the children (22.7% with elective needs and 32.5% with mandatory needs). The final model had an adequate fit: RMSEA = 0.03 (0.00-0.07), CFI = 0.97, TLI = 0.92 and SRMR = 0.03. Orthodontic treatment needs were influenced by dental caries (β: -0.011; p = 0.04), whereas parental oral health literacy was impacted by monthly family income (β: 0.36; p < 0.001) and maternal schooling (β: -0.041; p < 0.001). The structural equation model found no direct or indirect association between the level of oral health literacy of parents/guardians and orthodontic treatment needs of their children (p > 0.05). title: Estimating the causal effect of sugar consumption on dental decay: a longitudinal targeted maximum likelihood estimation study.
abstract: Dental decay in permanent teeth is the most prevalent disease worldwide, with 54% of young people under the age of 18 having experienced it. Despite these findings, there have been no studies that investigated the causal effects of time-varying exposure to higher sugar consumption throughout childhood on dental decay in late adolescence. We investigated the causal effects of sustained higher sugar consumption, cumulative sugar consumption, and sugar consumption trajectories from ages 4 to 14 on the risk of ever experiencing dental decay at age 16. We used data from the Longitudinal Study of Australian Children, an ongoing national Australian study that started in 2004, with a sample of 4671 young people. Causal effects were estimated using longitudinal targeted maximum likelihood estimation combined with the Super Learner ensemble. Young people with sustained higher sugar consumption (ie, above-median sugar consumption at ages 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14) throughout the study period had a 37 percentage point higher risk of dental decay compared to those with no exposure. Each additional exposure to higher sugar consumption (ie, additional above-median sugar consumption at a certain age) between ages 4 and 14 was associated with a 6% increase in the relative risk of dental decay by age 16. This study provides causal evidence linking higher sugar consumption throughout childhood to dental decay in late adolescence.

title: Effect of Image Enhancement Filters on the Detection of Periapical Radiolucent Lesions on Panoramic Radiographs: A Multi-Reader Multi-Case Study.
abstract: Background: Panoramic radiography is widely used in dental practice, but its two-dimensional projection geometry and anatomical superimposition can obscure periapical radiolucent lesions, particularly in the maxillary anterior region and for novice observers. Methods: This retrospective multi-reader, multi-case study aimed to evaluate the effects of unsharp mask and Gaussian blur filters on the diagnostic performance and interobserver agreement of novice observers in detecting periapical radiolucent lesions on panoramic radiographs. Twenty final-year dental students evaluated 56 panoramic radiographs (28 lesion-positive and 28 lesion-free cases; 224 maxillary anterior teeth) under three imaging conditions (original, unsharp mask, and Gaussian blur). Observers scored lesion presence using a five-point confidence scale. Diagnostic performance (AUC, sensitivity, and specificity) was compared using the Dorfman-Berbaum-Metz/Obuchowski-Rockette multi-reader, multi-case method. Interobserver agreement was assessed using quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: Imaging condition significantly affected AUC, sensitivity, and specificity (all p ≤ 0.003). Compared with original images, unsharp mask significantly improved sensitivity (78.2% vs. 52.5%), specificity (90.2% vs. 83.2%), and AUC (0.876 vs. 0.737) (all p < 0.05), with the highest interobserver agreement (ICC = 0.951; κ = 0.476). title: Interventions for managing immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
abstract: Rationale: Immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps are difficult candidates for conventional root canal fillings. Interventions for management of such teeth include regenerative endodontic procedures (REPs), apexification, and root strengthening interventions. Basic principles involve removal of necrotic pulp, canal debridement and infection control. Currently, there is no evidence-based guidance to manage such teeth. Objectives: To assess the effects of different interventions to manage immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps. Search Methods: We used CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Oral Health specialised register, and two trials registers, together with reference checking, to identify studies that were included in the review. The latest search date was October 2025. Eligibility Criteria: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing additions to autologous blood clot (BC) scaffolds in REPs with conventional BC scaffolds in REPs for managing necrotic pulps in immature permanent teeth in children. We also included RCTs comparing different additions to BC scaffolds, coronal sealing materials, and intracanal disinfectants in REPs, different approaches to apexification, REPS (using any approach) with apexification, and root strengthening interventions. title: Keratinised mucosa width and peri-implant disease during supportive peri-implant care: A follow-up analysis using cluster-adjusted sensitivity models in an established maintenance cohort.
journal: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)
abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the associations between keratinised mucosa width and peri-implant mucositis, peri-implantitis and peri-implant mucosal inflammation severity in patients receiving supportive peri-implant care. Materials And Methods: This observational follow-up analysis included patients re-examined between February and October 2020. Keratinised mucosa width was categorised a priori as 2 or ≥ 2 mm. The primary outcomes were peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis at follow-up; the secondary outcome was the mucositis severity score. Available radiographs taken previously were used to support the diagnostic classification. Primary cluster-adjusted generalised estimating equation models included keratinised mucosa width 2 mm, age, loading time, history of periodontitis, residual dentition status, smoking and approximal Plaque Index > 35%. Sensitivity analyses evaluated plaque-, prosthesis-, and anatomical/local phenotype-adjusted and patient-level worst-implant models. Results: This study included 500 implants from 104 patients. Peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis were diagnosed in 288 (57.6%) and 49 (9.8%) implants, respectively. Radiographs were available for 380 implants (76.0%) and supported diagnostic classification in 43 of 49 peri-implantitis cases (87.8%). title: Differential Gene Expression in Dental Pulp of Healthy and Symptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis Cases.
abstract: Introduction: Symptomatic irreversible pulpitis is characterized by persistent inflammation of the dental pulp, resulting in severe pain and eventual pulp necrosis if untreated. This study investigated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in dental pulp tissues of individuals with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis compared with healthy pulp, focusing on inflammation, angiogenesis, and tissue repair. Methods: Pulp samples were collected from patients with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis and from healthy controls undergoing elective root canal treatment. Total RNA was extracted, and high-quality samples (260/280 ratio 1.8-2.0) were subjected to RNA sequencing using the MGI platform. Differential expression analysis was performed with edgeR.. DEGs with log2 fold change (LFC) > 1 or < -1 and P < 0.05 were considered significant. Results: RNA sequencing identified distinct gene expression in symptomatic irreversible pulpitis compared with healthy pulp. Pro-inflammatory mediators such as gene IL6 (LFC = 2.3), TNF (LFC = 2.2), COX-2 (LFC = 2.3), CXCL8/IL-8 (LFC = 2.2), ZBP1 (LFC = 3.5), and RANKL (LFC = 2.6) were significantly upregulated, indicating immune activation and inflammatory signalling. Angiogenesis-related genes including ANGPT2 (LFC = 4.1), BMP7 (LFC = 3.9), and VEGF-A (LFC = 2.1) were also upregulated, suggesting vascular remodeling in response to tissue injury. title: Oral health behaviours and shift work barriers among Hungarian EMS personnel: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: Background: Shift-working emergency medical services (EMS) personnel face structural barriers to preventive oral care, yet national workforce data remain scarce. Objective: To estimate prevalence of oral symptoms, behaviours, dental attendance, and psychosocial OHRQoL impacts among Hungarian National Ambulance Service (OMSZ) staff; assess associations with occupational enablers/barriers; and evaluate acceptability of employer-supported screening. Methods: Nationwide cross-sectional anonymous online survey (13 Sep 2024-17 Apr 2025; n = 1,061; 73% men, 74% 24-hour shifts). Logistic regression examined a priori outcomes (ORs, 95% CI), adjusted for age/sex/attendance; STROBE-compliant. Results: Among 1,061 respondents, 74% reported 24-hour shifts as their primary duty pattern. Over half reported current or recent dental/oral problems (54.9%), and 20% had not attended a dental check-up within the previous two years. Off duty, 33% brushed twice daily, whereas during duty about two-thirds reported regular brushing. Workplace hygiene kits were reported by 40% of respondents and were more common among 24-hour shift workers. In regression analyses, kit availability was strongly associated with daily or more frequent on-duty brushing among 24-hour staff (85% vs. 21%). Daily brushing was associated with lower odds of toothache, non-use of interdental cleaning with higher odds of hiding teeth, and rare on-duty brushing with higher odds of halitosis. title: Prevalence and associated factors of infraocclusion in implant-supported fixed partial dentures: A cross-sectional observational study.
journal: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)
abstract: Purpose: A significant percentage of implant-supported fixed partial dentures develop complications, with implant infraocclusion being the most frequent. This study aims to analyse the prevalence of implant infraocclusion in fixed partial dentures and its potential associated factors, as well as to determine whether fixed partial dentures may have been placed according to an inadequate occlusal design. Materials And Methods: This cross-sectional observational study was conducted following the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines. The degree of implant infraocclusion in fixed partial dentures ≤ 4 units was visually assessed and additional variables were recorded. To identify factors independently associated with the presence of implant infraocclusion (> 0 mm), a multivariable logistic regression model based on generalised estimating equations was fitted. Results: A total of 409 patients (mean age 57.3 ± 12.8 years) with 1,012 implants were analysed. The overall prevalence of implant infraocclusion was 42.8%. The generalised estimating equation logistic regression model demonstrated significantly higher odds of implant infraocclusion when the antagonist was another implant (odds ratio 2.73; P 0.001), whereas fixed partial dentures in function for 5 years or less (odds ratio 0.60; P = 0.005) and treatment performed by the same professional (odds ratio 0.57; P = 0.010) were independently associated with lower odds of implant infraocclusi

title: Long-Term Fate of Resorbed Adjacent Teeth Associated With Impacted Maxillary Canines Following Orthodontic Treatment: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Limited evidence exists on the long-term prognosis of resorptive lesions in teeth adjacent to impacted maxillary canines' post-orthodontic treatment. To systematically evaluate the long-term radiographic status of resorbed maxillary incisor roots following orthodontic correction of adjacent ectopically erupting canines. Comprehensive electronic and manual searches across five databases identified retrospective or prospective studies assessing long-term Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) or radiographic follow-up of resorbed adjacent teeth. Data selection, extraction and bias assessment were performed independently. Five studies with moderate risk of bias met inclusion criteria. The combined sample consisted of 54 male and 123 female. Findings indicate that orthodontic management of impacted canines carries minimal risk of progressive root resorption or periodontal deterioration in adjacent incisors. Resorbed incisors largely retained vitality and functional stability, with no mobility beyond Grade 1 and resorption lacunae often became shallower over time. Marked heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Long-term outcomes are favourable, with most resorbed root surfaces showing natural remodelling and minimal need for endodontic intervention. title: Expert consensus on clinical practice in pterygoid implant rehabilitation: A modified Delphi study.
journal: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)
abstract: Purpose: Pterygoid implants provide distal anchorage in the atrophic posterior maxilla without sinus grafting, but protocols and implant designs vary widely. This study aimed to establish an experience-based consensus on pterygoid implant-anchored rehabilitation. Materials And Methods: The present authors conducted a two-round modified Delphi survey of 55 surgeons from 25 countries, each with over 5 years of experience and at least 50 pterygoid implants placed. Round 1 comprised 16 open-ended questions and thematic analysis produced 74 closed-ended items for Round 2. Consensus was defined a priori as agreement of at least 70% on a single option or on clinically equivalent options grouped in advance. Reporting followed the ACcurate COnsensus Reporting Document (ACCORD) and Conducting and REporting DElphi Studies (CREDES) guidelines. Results: All 55 panellists completed both rounds; mean agreement rose from 76% to 89%. Consensus was reached on mandatory CBCT (98%) and a single trajectory: entry distal to the second molar (82%), 30° to 50° posterior-superior angulation (91%), 15° to 35° medial angulation (87%) and an apex between the pterygoid plates (87%). The panel agreed on a tapered 16- to 22-mm implant with a narrow cutting apex and immediate loading when primary stability was adequate (89%); most panellists (62%) consistently required at least 45 Ncm insertion torque. title: Influence of posterior adjacent tooth presence, implant depth, and scanning strategies on trueness in partial edentulism.
abstract: Background: To evaluate the trueness of digital implant impressions in partially edentulous models according to posterior adjacent tooth presence, implant depth, and intraoral scanning strategy. Methods: Two maxillary models (Kennedy Class II Mod I) with implants at 1 mm (M1) and 3 mm (M3) subgingival depths were used. The left side retained the second molar, whereas the right side was edentulous. A confocal intraoral scanner was used with 4 strategies: right and left straight (RS, LS), and right and left zigzag (RZ, LZ). Each strategy was repeated 10 times (n = 80). Laboratory scans served as reference. Trueness was evaluated by root mean square (RMS), linear deviation of scan bodies, and inter-implant distance. Data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA (α = 0.05). Implants placed at 3 mm depth showed significantly higher deviations than those placed at 1 mm depth (p < 0.05). Straight scanning strategies resulted in lower deviations than zigzag strategies (p < 0.01). title: Assessment techniques for residual cement in cement-retained implant restorations: A systematic review.
abstract: Cement-retained implant restorations are popular because they offer aesthetic benefits and a good passive fit. However, residual subgingival cement is a frequent issue that can result in inflammation around the implant and potentially lead to its failure. This review aims to assess the data found in the literature on the techniques used to detect the cement residue in cement-retained implant restorations. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and EMBASE. The objective of the search strategy was to locate relevant studies, specifically in vitro studies, prospective cohort studies, retrospective studies, and randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that focus on the occurrence of excess cement in cement-retained implant restorations. The search was restricted to articles published from January 1, 2009, to December 31, 2023. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was utilised to assess the risk of bias for clinical studies (prospective, retrospective, and RCTs), whereas for in vitro studies, the QUADAS tool was employed to evaluate methodological quality. Out of 1842 study records screened, 25 studies met the inclusion criteria for the final analysis.
